name: Eliphelet
overview: Eliphelet is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Hashum who had married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:33. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes about him beyond this unique attribute. His mention highlights a particular family line involved in the post-exilic community's challenges with intermarriage.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliphelet means 'G-d [El] is [my] deliverance,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a clear declaration of trust in divine deliverance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eliphelet as a descendant of Hashum, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented apart from what is noted in his unique attribute.
scriptureSignificance: Eliphelet's significance lies in his representation of the post-exilic community's struggle with maintaining covenant purity, as his lineage includes a foreign wife, which was a critical issue addressed in Ezra. His mention underscores the challenges faced by Israel in adhering to God's commands about marriage and community holiness after the return from exile.
